text:
Sandra: Heads-up — I can repro an access-control issue. After last night's RBAC refactor deploy, some users scoped to project_viewer are seeing org-level cost/usage pages. Steps: log in as project_viewer@acme -> Console -> Cost Insights -> sees full org breakdown and other projects.
Alex: Yikes. Which deploy rolled that?
Sandra: deploy-bot shows: deployed rbac-service@v2.3.1 (commit 9f4a2b) at 1934999000. I noticed it ~10:30 UTC.
deploy-bot: rbac-service@v2.3.1 deployed to prod by CI (rollout: gradual).
Jin: Ok grabbing logs and role mappings now. Can you paste repro creds (throwaway) or exact API call?
Sandra: I used a test account (project_viewer) created via /admin/test-users. Repro via web console but same behavior calling API: GET /api/v1/analytics/usage?scope=project&project_id=acme-1 returns org-level rows.
Alex: Share recent migration/PR link?
Sandra: PR refactor: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/457. Main change: collapse role scopes into a single matcher that defaults to org when no explicit project mapping exists.
Jin: Querying DB:
```
SELECT id, role, scope_type, scope_id, created_at FROM role_bindings WHERE role='project_viewer' AND deleted=false LIMIT 5;
```
Results: a binding existed with scope_type='org' for a legacy service account (svc-metrics-ingest). That binding should have been project-scoped. Looks like the refactor canonicalized scope to 'org' for any binding missing project_id.
Maria: Could KMS rotation / audit pipeline changes have affected detection? We encrypt audit payloads with key audit-kms-v1; rotation happened last week but shouldn't change auth checks.
Sam: Likely a data-migration/normalization bug from PR 457 where unspecified scope mapped to org. Short-term mitigation: remove the erroneous binding and roll back the rollout of rbac-service@v2.3.1 for prod. Medium-term: add explicit validation and unit tests for scope normalization.
Jin: I'll remove the binding now and push a hotfix. Runbook steps I'm taking: 1) snapshot role_bindings, 2) delete offending binding, 3) restart rbac-service pod to pick up cache clear, 4) audit query to find other malformed rows.
Jin: running snapshot:
```
pg_dump -t role_bindings --data-only --column-inserts > /tmp/role_bindings_snapshot.sql
```
Jin: issuing delete:
```
DELETE FROM role_bindings WHERE id='rb-77f3' AND scope_type='org' AND role='project_viewer';
```
Sandra: After delete + pod restart I can no longer reproduce. Thanks.
Alex: We should check for other bindings that lost project_id during migration. Query suggestion:
```
SELECT id, created_at, payload->'legacy_scope' AS legacy FROM role_bindings WHERE scope_type='org' AND role IN ('project_viewer','project_editor') AND created_at > '2025-01-01';
```
Sam: Add follow-ups: 1) Jin to open a postmortem + label as P1 access exposure. 2) Devex to add e2e test that spins up a project_viewer and asserts no org-level cost rows. 3) Security to add an automated audit rule alerting when project-scoped roles are present with scope_type='org' and role looks like project_*. 4) Consider KMS audit log retention check — ensure we keep raw audit payloads (encrypted) for 90 days to reconstruct.
Jin: Created ticket SEC-1724: "RBAC refactor normalized missing scope -> org, exposing cost analytics" and assigned to me. ETA for hotfix: 2 hours.
Maria: Also double-check client-side console caching — we should invalidate any cached analytics view for sessions after RBAC change.
Sam: Good catch. Also flag to compliance: potential data exposure of cost breakdowns. We need to send a short incident notice to legal if affected customers >1.
audit-bot: Audit entries for role change/deletion recorded: event_id=e-992311, actor=Jin, affected=rb-77f3, timestamp=1935012405. (encrypted with audit-kms-v1)
Sandra: Actionables confirmed. Jin will roll back if we see additional regressions. I'll coordinate customer outreach if the count >1.
Alex: For the PR fix, ensure migration scripts set explicit scope_id or fail loudly. We'll also add a pre-deploy DB check in CI to fail if role_bindings rows without scope_id exist when upgrading.
Sam: Thanks team. Keep updates here. :lock: :eyes:
